signature: safe_text(text: str, encoding: str | None) -> str
requires: text is str and encoding is either None or a Python codec name supplied by the destination text stream.
Machine-readable callers serialize structured values before passing text to this boundary.
Callers retain stdout for protocol/output data and stderr for diagnostics.
ensures: If text is encodable by the declared encoding, the exact Unicode text is returned unchanged.
If one or more code points are not encodable, only those code points are replaced by deterministic ASCII backslash escapes and the returned text is encodable by the declared codec.
If encoding is None, UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32, Unicode text is preserved unchanged.
JSON command surfaces emit valid ASCII-safe JSON with ensure_ascii enabled, stable key ordering where the surface is canonical, and no locale-dependent replacement characters.
Human command surfaces preserve Turkish text on capable streams and expose unsupported glyphs as reversible backslash escapes on constrained streams.
CLI, discovery CLI, MCP startup diagnostics, dispatcher diagnostics, and redirected output use the same boundary rather than changing global process encodings.
The function is idempotent for a fixed encoding.
raises: Non-string text or non-string/non-null encoding is rejected as a programmer error.
An unknown codec name raises LookupError and is not guessed from locale.
Filesystem, broken-pipe, closed-stream, and other non-encoding I/O errors remain visible to the owning command boundary.

effects.process: none; never reconfigures sys.stdout, sys.stderr, locale, PYTHONIOENCODING, or global codec handlers
effects.repository: never edits source, contracts, PLAN, TODO, or PROGRESS

determinism.escaping: Python backslashreplace semantics with lowercase hexadecimal escapes define unsupported code points
determinism.locale: only the explicit stream encoding affects the returned text
determinism.json: machine output never depends on terminal glyph support
determinism.paths: no absolute checkout path is introduced

budget.time: linear in the number of Unicode code points plus codec conversion cost
budget.memory: at most one encoded byte representation and one decoded fallback string
budget.output_growth: each unsupported code point expands only to its standard backslash escape

epistemics.exact: the destination codec represents every code point and the returned string is unchanged
epistemics.escaped: unsupported code points are visibly and reversibly escaped without changing surrounding representable text
epistemics.machine_readable: JSON parses to the same data regardless of console encoding
epistemics.error: an invalid codec or non-encoding I/O failure is not hidden

invariants: Encoding fallback never drops text, substitutes an ambiguous question mark, or emits an unencodable result.
Representable Turkish characters are preserved under cp1254.
ASCII, cp1252, cp1254, UTF-8, and encoding-less redirected streams are covered by tests.
JSON stdout remains parseable and MCP stdout remains free of diagnostics.
No command mutates global locale or standard-stream configuration.
Successful UTF-8 output remains byte-compatible with the frozen legacy corpus unless a separate bug fix is documented.
